recipes.name: Black Beans and Rice
ingredients_raw: 1.5 cups low sodium, low fat vegetable broth

steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Add onion; cook and stir until onion has softened, about 3 minutes.
Add rice, garlic, salt, cumin, and cayenne. Cook and stir for 2 to 3 minutes to lightly toast the rice and warm the spices until fragrant.
Add vegetable broth and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender, about 20 minutes.
Stir in black beans and cook until warmed through, 2 to 3 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Black Beans and Rice
raw_recipe.description: Black beans and rice flavored with garlic, cumin, and cayenne pepper makes a wholesome, budget-friendly, vegetarian meal or tasty side dish.

review.reviewBody: This recipe was excellent. However, I did follow other's advice. I added 1 can tomatoes w/chiles, 1 can of corn, 1 can of beans, 2tsp cumin, 2 tsp tumeric, splash of lime, chicken broth. This will definitely be added to my menu.
Great recipe! The only addition I made was some diced tomatos and extra garlic. Great tortilla filling! Even my meat-eater hubby loved it!

I am rating the recipe as written 4-stars - but with a few minor changes it quickly becomes a 5-star recipe! I made the following changes: 1 tsp granulated garlic instead of 2 cloves (non in the house), chicken broth instead of veggie, 2 tsp cumin, only 1 can of black beans, plus added 1 can of corn (drained) and 1 can of Rotel tomatoes (undrained). My husband loved it and has asked that it be added to our menu on a regular basis. We used it as a burrito filling, a quesadilla filling, and a stand-alone dish. I also added extra chicken broth to some of the leftovers and made it into soup. The mixture would also be good on top of nachos or combined with chicken and cheese to make a casserole. Cheese and/or sour cream are good compliments. Next time, I will lower the cayenne to 1/8 tsp (the Rotel adds enough heat for my taste) and use 2 cans of beans (black, pinto, and kidney would all work well in this dish).

I have made this several times. I add 1/4 tsp of turmeric and I get a delicious yellow color. I use half the beans and serve this as a side dish. I rinse the rice until the water is clear, that way I get perfect fluffy rice every time, just like my favorite mexican restaurant.

I made this even quicker, I used my power pressure cooker. Sautéed onions, garlic and rice. Placed all of the other ingredients into the inner pot. (I used regular long grain rice) I despise instant rice. Set it on the Rice button (which is 7 min. On high. Quick release, stirred and served. It was perfect!

I did make some changes. I put one 15 ounce can of black beans in, I think 3 cups would be too many for us. I didn’t put cayenne or cumin in it, as I also added a 10 ounce can of diced tomatoes with green chilies, lime juice and cilantro and I was worried about how spicy it would be. It’s still a bit hot for me. I added some cut up shrimp that I had. My husband liked it, but he spiced it up with some salsa. I added some sour cream and ate it on a low carb tortilla. My husband just came back for seconds!

I had never made this type of dish before but I read all the reviews and this is what I did: substituted the veg broth for chicken broth, added 1/2 cup diced celery and one chopped carrot to the onion at the start, added 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tsp chili powder in addition to the recipe spices. After the 20 minutes cooking time, added 1 can Rotel tomatoes with chili's, 1 can drained corn and 1 can black beans, 1 tsp cilantro and a 1/2 tsp lime juice, and allowed to heat through on low until everything was hot and tender.I am not a huge spicy food person and this was just on the brink of too hot, but I loved it! You could add cooked chicken or fish or sausage at the end. I served it in a tortilla with pulled pieces of rotisserie chicken and shredded cheese and a dollop of sour cream.....to die for!!!

I substituted the broth with a can of tomato soup, and it worked out fine. I doubled the garlic. Instead of a stock pot on the stove, I used my electric pressure cooker. Started on Sauté High mode and then switched to Pressure Cooker Rice mode. I let it vent naturally and afterwards stirred in the beans and spices in Keep Warm mode. An easy, versatile recipe.

I thought this was very easy. I added paprika and turmeric with the onions and garlic. I forgot to cover it so needed to add more broth. Finishes it with cheddar cheese and a sprinkling of green onions.

Definitely needed some doctoring up, but it was really good and VERY easy to pull together. (I’ve already had three bowls of it today, lol.) I didn’t have an onion but I did have green onions so used them instead, sautéed the thinly sliced whites in the olive oil with jarred garlic. Since I didn’t have enough onions I made Lipton onion soup and scooped the onions off the top and added to the sautéed onions in the pan, then added the rice to coat, then added one cup chicken bone broth and 1/2 the Lipton onion soup, brought it to a boil and then followed the recipe as stated. I did add some turmeric at the end as well. It needed salt for reals. The first bowl I added a little Sriracha (spelled wrong) and green onions. The second bowl a bit of butter and salt. The third bowl just salt and green onions. I took a lot of liberties for lack of ingredients, but it’s easy to make this dish your own. (Especially if you’re on a strict budget and have to make do with what you have to work with.) Very good!

Fine recipe as is but I then started making it my own. Separately fried a pound of hamburger with taco seasoning. Added green pepper to the onion. After rice was cooked I added the ground beef, a small can of corn and a small can of diced tomatoes. Served with cheese and sour cream and nacho chips/taco shells.
I loved these beans. They were even better the next day. I did up the cumin quite a bit.
I made it as listed except it’s a few less beans. Tastes wonderful!

I love black beans and rice. I made it exactly as the recipe. I like chopped raw onions on top so i didn’t cook them. I love the simplicity of this meal and it’s definitely great as a main dish for me. I don’t add the tomatoes &other things some of the reviewers did. If they ever tried your recipe as is they wouldn’t bother creating a completely different dish. 🙄😂
We love this healthy dish

The Simplicity of it hides the Great Taste and ease of preparation. I've been using this recipe for a couple years now and have only finally taken a moment, shame on me, to say how extraordinary it truly is.
I made this exactly like the recipe as I had all ingredients on hand. It's excellent! I put guacamole chips and jalapeños on the side.
I’ve made this recipe many times. It’s easy and inexpensive. I’m debating on adding a jalapeño pepper that I just pulled off my plant. I don’t want to ruin the dish though.

This is the first beans and rice recipe I've tried in a long time that I really liked. I made two changes. I used a wild rice blend instead of white rice and I added about 1/2 teaspoon of liquid smoke, just so I could finish off the bottle and throw it away. The dish was excellent. I can see the additions below being tasty as well, but I loved it in its simple form.
Great flavour very easy to make i did not have any veg stock so i used chicken stock i will most definitely make it again
